comparator.name: Psychology (Psychologie)
comparator.sourceNotes: The current student curriculum establishes a 180-EC bachelor with 75 EC of compulsory major study, 60 EC of major choices and 45 EC of genuine profiling space. The compulsory major consists of eight first-year courses (60 EC) and a 15-EC bachelor research project. The coherent selected major-choice pathway uses the two first-listed thematic courses in their respective blocks, the first two listed research-skills trainings, compulsory Advanced Research Methods and Statistics, and three clinical-scientific theory courses. These choices total 60 EC. The generic target names no domain; the three domains are equally formal and may overlap, so the first-listed Clinical Scientific domain is selected by neutral official order. The 45-EC profiling space remains generic rather than being filled with invented subjects.

comparatorRouteSelection.basis: The normalized target is the generic broad Psychology bachelor. Utrecht groups later major choices into Clinical Scientific, Societal Scientific and Fundamental Scientific domains, allows overlap, and does not designate one as the general route. The first-listed Clinical Scientific domain is therefore selected as a neutral official-order tie-break, independently of UCR fit. Within the required thematic and research-skills choices, first-listed options are used in published order.

alternativeSelection.assessment: The broad closest match covers Utrecht’s programme-wide psychology and research core. Brain and cognition and social and organisational psychology are independently evidenced, coherent, mechanically feasible and substantively distinct additional routes. Clinical/mental-health and developmental directions were also assessed, but three UCR alternatives is the maximum.

comparisonAlignment.rationale: Both courses provide a foundation in social-psychological theory, social cognition and group behaviour.
Both courses study cognitive, social and emotional development across the lifespan.
Utrecht’s disciplinary philosophy-and-science course has no single one-to-one UCR counterpart.
Both introduce brain function, behaviour and the interaction of biological and psychological explanation.
Both introduce psychopathology, individual differences and clinical explanation.
Both address complex cognitive functions including memory, language and decision-making.
The selected Utrecht clinical-theory course is more specialized than any one selected UCR course.
Utrecht’s dedicated clinical-neuropsychology course has no one-to-one selected UCR counterpart.
Utrecht’s dedicated clinical-developmental course has no one-to-one selected UCR counterpart.
Both advance psychological research design and statistical analysis beyond the introductory level.
Both develop advanced psychological research design, analysis and critical interpretation.
Both introduce research design, measurement and descriptive and inferential statistics.
Both use computational tools to analyse and visualize data, although Utrecht’s training is specifically in Python.
The integrated Utrecht thematic course on motivation and self-regulation has no one-to-one selected UCR counterpart.
The integrated Utrecht thematic course on technology, identity and wellbeing has no one-to-one selected UCR counterpart.
Utrecht’s dedicated experiment-building training has no one-to-one selected UCR counterpart.
The compulsory 15-EC Utrecht bachelor research project has no one-to-one selected UCR course with the same role and credit structure.
Genuine profiling space is not assigned a particular UCR counterpart.

notes.text: Utrecht Psychology provides a structured disciplinary sequence with dedicated psychological methods, research-skills trainings, clinical theory and a supervised 15-EC bachelor project. UCR can build substantial psychology, cognition and organisational programmes, but it does not reproduce the same specialist practical sequence or professional clinical preparation.
